description: One auditable record entry for a noted or challenged data-span claim. Records are append-only: one JSON object per line in a records file, written once and never edited after the fact. Field order is stable and every record carries the span's SHA-256, so a records file can be hash-chained into a ledger the same way this suite's other artifacts are.

action_taken.description: What was done, in plain words: for a challenge, that the claim was refused authority and how it was escalated; for a note, that it was recorded only.

check_fired.description: The primary check that fired, in the screener's 'family:detail' form (for example 'contradiction:record-suppression'), or the note reason for a noted record.

checks_fired.description: Every check that fired, in firing order, when more than the primary check is worth keeping. Optional; 'check_fired' is always the first of these when both are present.

claim_text.description: The claim as extracted: the instruction-shaped segment addressed to the agent, quoted as written.

source_class.description: The harness-assigned class of the span the claim was found in. Principal classes are listed for completeness; in practice only data spans produce records, because principal spans are instructions, not claims.

source_id.description: The harness's identifier for the source the span came from (a fixture id, a tool-call id, a file path, a retrieval URL) — enough to find the span again.

span_hash.description: SHA-256 of the span's exact text, prefixed with 'sha256:'.

timestamp.description: When the record was written, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

verdict.description: 'challenge': an agent-directed claim a check fired on, or any uncorroborated agent-directed claim — never obeyed. 'note': instruction-shaped data that is not agent-directed, or a claim with local quotation/documentation framing — recorded, usable as data, no escalation.

title: Message-security challenge record
